assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational account of how collateral and balance sheets amplify macroeconomic fluctuations, with enduring influence on macro-finance and policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore supply the central collateral mechanism, while Gertler is a principal architect of the financial-accelerator framework.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have been extensively developed, tested, and incorporated into mainstream macroeconomic models over decades.
uncertainties: The broad literature makes the boundary between the core mechanism and subsequent contributors difficult to draw.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work made liquidity and funding constraints central to the understanding of asset prices, market stress, and financial stability.
assessment.attribution: Amihud's liquidity measure and Brunnermeier's and Pedersen's theoretical contributions form a credible, complementary core.
assessment.maturity: The framework has become deeply embedded in empirical asset pricing and analyses of financial crises.
uncertainties: Liquidity research is broad, so a prize formulation would need to delimit the contribution carefully.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection transformed modern trade theory and sharpened measurement of the consequences of globalization.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is indispensable to the core model; Helpman and Redding represent major related theoretical development.
assessment.maturity: The approach has generated a large theoretical and empirical literature and remains a standard organizing framework.
uncertainties: Attribution among the many contributors to heterogeneous-firm trade is inherently difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The legal-origins research program established investor protection and legal institutions as central explanations for financial development and corporate governance.
assessment.attribution: La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, and Shleifer are core authors of the defining empirical program.
assessment.maturity: The work has had long-lasting influence across finance, development, and law and economics.
uncertainties: The causal interpretation and universality of legal-origin claims remain contested.
Robert W. Vishny is also a central collaborator.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods supplied widely used tools for credible empirical work with persistent outcomes and endogenous regressors.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell, and Bond have clear and closely connected claims to the central estimators and their application.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been intensively used, assessed, and refined over many years.
uncertainties: Their practical use can be fragile when instruments proliferate or assumptions are weak.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data made intergenerational mobility measurable at unprecedented scale and changed research and public discussion of opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman are central to the data-driven mobility research program.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been replicated, extended, and used to study mechanisms and policy-relevant geographic variation.
uncertainties: The appropriate interpretation of mobility measures and the role of causal mechanisms remain debated.
Lawrence F. Katz also has an important claim to credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on reciprocity, fairness, and inequity aversion changed the modeling of incentives, contracts, and cooperation.
assessment.attribution: Fehr and Schmidt provide a seminal formalization, while Falk has been a central empirical and experimental contributor.
assessment.maturity: The evidence and theory have influenced behavioral, labor, organizational, and contract economics for decades.
uncertainties: The empirical stability and external scope of particular social-preference measures remain uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work clarified how household leverage, mortgage credit, and indebtedness can propagate severe macroeconomic downturns.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are the central empirical architects; Campbell's work provides an important household-finance foundation.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has shaped research on the global financial crisis and the macroeconomic consequences of household balance sheets.
uncertainties: The relative importance of household debt versus other crisis mechanisms varies across settings.
